data.name: 4E-BP1
data.description: Translational repressor; the master effector through which mTORC1 controls protein synthesis. mTORC1 phosphorylates 4E-BP1 to release eIF4E and switch translation ON.
data.description_beginner: A protein that holds the translation-starter eIF4E hostage - until mTORC1 phosphorylates it, releasing eIF4E and switching protein production on. It's the main effector through which mTORC1 controls how much protein a cell makes.

studies.title: A unifying model for mTORC1-mediated regulation of mRNA translation
studies.authors: Thoreen CC; Chantranupong L; Keys HR; Wang T; Gray NS; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Used ribosome profiling with the complete inhibitor Torin1 to address a long-standing debate: in these cells, mTORC1's translational control runs largely through the 4E-BP family acting on a specific class of mRNAs (TOP motifs). Losing just the 4E-BPs makes translation of TOP mRNAs resistant to mTOR inhibition - naming them the master effectors.

studies.title: The translational landscape of mTOR signalling steers cancer initiation and metastasis
studies.authors: Hsieh AC; Liu Yi; Edlind MP; Ingolia NT; Janes MR; Sher A; et al.; Ruggero D

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Showed WHY mTOR-driven translation matters for cancer: in prostate cancer, oncogenic mTOR selectively translates a specific set of pro-invasion mRNAs that drive metastasis. An ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor (INK128) reversed that signature - an early preclinical rationale from mouse models and cell lines, not a clinical result.

studies.title: An ATP-competitive mammalian target of rapamycin inhibitor reveals rapamycin-resistant functions of mTORC1
studies.authors: Thoreen CC; Kang SA; Chang JW; Liu Q; Zhang Jianming; Gao Y; Reichling LJ; Sim T; Sabatini DM; Gray NS

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Dropped a bombshell: rapamycin does NOT fully block mTORC1. Using Torin1 (which jams the active site directly), the authors showed rapamycin leaves important mTORC1 jobs running - notably 4E-BP1 phosphorylation and autophagy suppression. This reframed a decade of rapamycin experiments and launched the search for complete inhibitors.

studies.title: mTOR regulates the pro-tumorigenic senescence-associated secretory phenotype by promoting IL1A translation
studies.authors: Laberge RM; Sun Y; Orjalo AV; Patil CK; Freund A; et al.; Campisi J

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Explained HOW rapamycin calms 'inflammaging'. Senescent cells spew inflammatory signals (the SASP) that damage surrounding tissue and even feed tumors. mTOR powers this by translating IL1A, the cytokine at the top of the cascade. Rapamycin selectively shuts it down - and blocked senescent cells from fueling prostate tumor growth in mice.

studies.title: 4E-BP extends lifespan upon dietary restriction by enhancing mitochondrial activity in Drosophila
studies.authors: Zid BM; Rogers AN; Katewa SD; Vargas MA; Kolipinski MC; Lu TA; Benzer S; Kapahi P

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Connected the dots between diet, mTOR, and lifespan. 4E-BP, an mTOR target, is upregulated on dietary restriction and here was shown to be REQUIRED for the lifespan boost, working by selectively boosting translation of mitochondrial genes. A rare case pinning a specific mTOR effector to the longevity benefit of eating less.

studies.title: The Bi-steric, mTORC1-Selective Inhibitor, RMC-5552, in Advanced Solid Tumors: A Phase 1 Trial
studies.authors: Schram AM; Meyerowitz JG et al.

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human (Phase 1 dose escalation, n=57, advanced solid tumors, NCT04774952)
studies.finding: First-in-human, open-label dose-escalation trial (n=57, advanced solid tumors, no comparator arm) of a bi-steric mTORC1-selective inhibitor. Treatment-related hyperglycemia was low (4%) and not dose-limiting, alongside a 64% disease control rate. Because the trial was uncontrolled and made no head-to-head comparison against rapamycin or an ATP-site inhibitor, this is encouraging early clinical evidence consistent with the hypothesis that sparing mTORC2 reduces metabolic toxicity -- it does not establish mTORC2 sparing as the cause.

studies.title: A bi-steric mTORC1-selective inhibitor overcomes drug resistance in breast cancer
studies.authors: Meng D; Bandyopadhyay S et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human ER+/HER2- breast cancer cell lines; mouse patient-derived xenografts (PDX)
studies.finding: RMC-6272, a bi-steric molecule with >25-fold selectivity for mTORC1 over mTORC2, completely suppresses mTORC1 (hitting the rapamycin-resistant substrate 4E-BP1) and overcomes hormone- and CDK4/6-inhibitor resistance in breast cancer cell lines and PDX -- the preclinical basis for the RMC-5552 selective-inhibitor clinical program.

studies.title: Sexual Dimorphism in Placental mTORC1 Signaling, Amino Acid Transport, and Mitochondrial Respiration at Term.
studies.authors: Shimada H; Sakuragi T; Zaegel V et al.

evidence.label: Human study
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: In 46 term placentas, male placentas showed higher mTORC1 signalling (increased S6RP phosphorylation, reduced 4E-BP1), greater System A amino acid transport and higher mitochondrial respiratory capacity than female placentas, and male pregnancies had a higher birth-weight-to-placental-weight ratio. Observational: a cross-sectional association at a single timepoint, with no intervention and no randomisation, so the direction of the relationship between mTORC1 signalling and growth is not established here and residual confounding by maternal and obstetric factors cannot be excluded.

studies.title: Ku-0063794 is a specific inhibitor of the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR)
studies.authors: Garcia-Martinez JM; Alessi DR et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Ku-0063794 is a specific ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor blocking mTORC1 and mTORC2.

studies.title: Lsp2 links mTORC1 to TOP mRNA translation and lifespan in Drosophila
studies.authors: Wang J; Cai Z; Gu J; Xiong S; Yi J; Yang M; Chang K; Ning X; Wen Y; Yan Y; Lu J; Wang Y; Zhai Z

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Drosophila melanogaster — Lsp2 genetic ablation, lifespan assay, translatomic (ribosome profiling) analysis
studies.finding: Identifies Lsp2, a Drosophila fat-body storage protein, as an amino-acid-induced feedback activator of mTORC1 that specifically boosts translation of TOP-motif mRNAs (mostly ribosomal proteins) via 4E-BP — a rapamycin-resistant arm of mTORC1 output. Genetic loss of Lsp2 reduces TOP mRNA translation and robustly extends lifespan without cost to reproduction, revealing a rapamycin-independent route from mTORC1 activity to organismal longevity.

studies.title: Regulation of 4E-BP1 phosphorylation: a novel two-step mechanism
studies.authors: Gingras AC; Sonenberg N et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: 4E-BP1 is phosphorylated by an ordered, priming two-step mechanism that controls its release of eIF4E.

studies.title: mTORC1 phosphorylation sites encode their sensitivity to starvation and rapamycin
studies.authors: Kang SA; Pacold ME; Cervantes CL; Lim D; Lou HJ; Ottina K; Gray NS; Turk BE; Yaffe MB; Sabatini DM

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human and mouse cell lines; in vitro mTORC1 kinase assays on peptide substrates
studies.finding: Each mTORC1 phosphorylation site has its own intrinsic 'substrate quality'. Good substrates stay phosphorylated when mTORC1 is partly inhibited by rapamycin or starvation, poor ones drop out first, and changing a few residues around a site shifts its sensitivity in cells. One level of mTORC1 activity can therefore produce different output profiles.

studies.title: Mammalian cell size is controlled by mTOR and its downstream targets S6K1 and 4EBP1/eIF4E
studies.authors: Fingar DC; Blenis J et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: mTOR controls mammalian cell size through its downstream translational targets S6K1 and 4E-BP1/eIF4E.

studies.title: Amino acid sufficiency and mTOR regulate p70 S6 kinase and eIF-4E BP1 through a common effector mechanism
studies.authors: Hara K; Avruch J et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Amino acid sufficiency signals through mTOR to p70 S6K and 4E-BP1 via a common effector, first linking nutrients to mTOR.

studies.title: Phosphorylation of the translational repressor PHAS-I by the mammalian target of rapamycin
studies.authors: Brunn GJ; Abraham RT et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: mTOR directly phosphorylates 4E-BP1 (PHAS-I), releasing eIF4E and establishing mTOR's role in translational control.

studies.title: The mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) partner, raptor, binds the mTOR substrates p70 S6 kinase and 4E-BP1 through their TOR signaling (TOS) motif
studies.authors: Nojima H; Yonezawa K et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Raptor binds mTOR substrates via their TOS motifs, acting as the substrate-presenting scaffold of mTORC1.

relations.mechanism: Unphosphorylated 4E-BP1 clamps onto eIF4E and stops it assembling the cap-binding complex. mTORC1 phosphorylates 4E-BP1 to release that grip - so the brake on translation is released, not the accelerator pressed.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Untagged 4E-BP1 clamps onto eIF4E and blocks it; mTORC1 tags 4E-BP1 to make it let go – releasing a brake, not pressing an accelerator.

relations.mechanism: Keeping 4E-BP active extends lifespan under dietary restriction in flies, by enhancing mitochondrial activity. One of the few places where a single downstream node, not the whole pathway, carries the lifespan effect.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Keeping 4E-BP switched on extends lifespan in fruit flies on a restricted diet, by protecting their mitochondria.
relations.boundary: Fly only, and only under dietary restriction - the effect was not seen on a full diet.
relations.note: Boundary condition matters more than the headline here.

relations.mechanism: In mammalian cells (MOR2013) 4E-BPs repress translation of nucleus-encoded mitochondrial mRNAs, so mTORC1 raises mitochondrial output by inhibiting them; this arm is less rapamycin-sensitive than the S6K arm. In flies on dietary restriction (ZID2009) upregulated 4E-BP instead enhances translation of mitochondrial respiratory mRNAs. The sign depends on organism and nutrient state, so it is drawn as conditional.
relations.mechanism_beginner: The 4E-BP branch helps set how many mitochondrial proteins get built. In mammalian cells it holds them back; in fruit flies on a restricted diet it boosts them, so the direction depends on the organism and the diet.
relations.boundary: Scope: mammalian cells, MOR2013. The sign holds where 4E-BP represses translation of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial mRNAs (TFAM, mitochondrial ribosomal proteins), which is why this branch survives rapamycin better than the S6K arm. It does NOT hold universally across species and nutrient states: in Drosophila under dietary restriction, ZID2009 reports that 4E-BP ENHANCES mitochondrial activity, and that this is how it extends lifespan. Treat the mammalian-cell direction as scoped, not general.
relations.note: ZID2009 is recorded as conflicting evidence on this edge (moved out of the supporting list on 2026-08-30): its own title says 4E-BP ENHANCES mitochondrial activity under dietary restriction in flies, which is the opposite sign to this mammalian-cell edge.

relations.mechanism: mTORC1 phosphorylates 4E-BP1, which lets go of eIF4E and frees cap-dependent translation. Rapamycin blocks this arm only partially - the origin of the whole 'rapamycin-resistant output' problem.
relations.mechanism_beginner: mTORC1 tags 4E-BP1 so it lets go of another protein, freeing up protein-building – but the standard drug (rapamycin) only partly blocks this step.
